official.deadline_note: The official page publishes month-level timing only: NIIED announces the programme in September, Embassy Track applications are submitted in September and University Track applications run September to November, screening and selection run October to December, and final results are announced by NIIED in December. No day-level deadline is published on the page.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle announced by NIIED each September
official.status_note: The page publishes the application windows as Embassy Track September and University Track September to November, so as of the verification date the University Track window is the current one; the 'Apply for the GKS' control on the page returned the message 'It is not the application period.' when checked, which concerns the Study in Korea online route used by the Embassy Track.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Scholarship Benefits as published: 'Airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition, and monthly allowances.'
eligibility: Nationality: Applicants and both of their parents must hold non-Korean citizenship
Age: Applicants must be under 25 years of age as of the applicable year
Education: Associate Degree Program - High school graduate or expected to graduate; Bachelor's Degree Program - High school or associate degree graduate or expected to graduate

Academic Performance: Applicants must meet the academic performance requirements, such as a cumulative score of 80% or higher, ranking within the top 20% of their class, or meeting the required CGPA threshold
Embassy Track General and Overseas Korean applicants may apply to up to three universities, including at least one Type B university; R-GKS applicants may apply to up to two Type B universities
requirements: Korean language training (1 year) plus the degree program
Embassy Track: apply online through Study in Korea (www.studyinkorea.go.kr)
University Track: apply directly to a GKS-designated university
Detailed information on universities and academic departments can be found in the 'University Information File' available for download from the GKS announcements
For detailed information, please refer to the application guidelines and announcements posted in the GKS notices
selection_criteria: Embassy Track: screened and selected by the Korean embassy/consulate, then NIIED, then the university
University Track: screened and selected by the university, then NIIED
Final results are announced by NIIED in December
application_method: Read the eligibility criteria and choose a track (Embassy Track General, Embassy Track Overseas Koreans, Embassy Track R-GKS, University Track UIC, or University Track Associate Degree)
Embassy Track: apply online through Study in Korea
University Track: apply directly to a GKS university
Submit within the published track window and await screening and selection
official.application_route: Embassy Track applies online through Study in Korea (studyinkorea.go.kr); University Track applies directly to a GKS-designated university.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants and both of their parents must hold non-Korean citizenship.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme invites outstanding international students; the applicant and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The General Program covers various fields such as humanities, social studies, natural sciences, and arts and physical education; Specialization (UIC) covers science and engineering departments and is available only for associate and bachelor's degree programs.
official.duration: Korean language training (1 year) + associate degree programs (2-3 years), bachelor's degree programs (4-6 years)
official.description: This is a government-invited scholarship degree program aimed at fostering global talent and establishing international networks by inviting outstanding students from around the world. The Korean government provides international students with opportunities to study and offers various scholarship programs, funding one year of Korean language training followed by a degree at one of the GKS universities.

verification.notes: Read the awarding body's own page (NIIED Study in Korea) in full on 2026-10-10; benefits wording, selection quota of 286 undergraduate places, track structure, eligibility criteria and the month-level schedule are confirmed as published; the page states no monetary amount and no day-level deadline, and the linked GKS user-guide PDF could not be parsed for text.

applicant_utility.summary: GKS Undergraduate is a two-route Korean government scholarship: the Embassy Track applies through the Korean embassy in your country during September, while the University Track (UIC and Associate Degree) is a direct application to a designated GKS university in a September-November window, and both feed into NIIED selection with results in December. Every awardee does a compulsory one-year Korean language course before the degree starts. NIIED publishes no monetary value for the monthly allowance on this page, so the actual stipend figure only becomes available in the annual GKS announcement guidelines, and the department-level detail lives in the downloadable University Information File rather than the overview page.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent high-school graduates under 25 who are non-Korean citizens (both parents included) with an 80%-or-top-20% academic record and who want a government-funded degree in Korea including a language year.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm that you and both of your parents hold non-Korean citizenship before anything else
Check you will still be under 25 in the intake year and gather transcripts showing 80% or higher, top-20% class rank, or the equivalent CGPA

Decide your track early: Embassy Track (online through Study in Korea) or University Track (direct to a listed GKS university), including at least one Type B university for Embassy General and Overseas Korean applicants
Download the University Information File from the GKS announcement for department-level detail before choosing your universities
Plan for a compulsory one-year Korean language training programme before your degree begins
common_rejection_risks: Applying only to Type A universities when the Embassy Track rules require at least one Type B choice
Missing a University Track window that is set by each university individually, not by a single NIIED deadline
Falling below the published academic-performance threshold (80% cumulative, top 20% of class, or required CGPA)
Assuming the online Study in Korea application also covers the University Track, when that route is a direct application to the university
document_audit: The page publishes no document checklist; the required document set appears only in the annual GKS announcement guidelines and the University Information File, so do not rely on last year's list
Embassy Track applicants apply online through Study in Korea and must follow the announcement's document rules exactly
alerts: By mid-October the Embassy Track submission month (September) has passed for this cycle; the University Track September-November window is the live one

The undergraduate quota is fixed at 286 places (156 Embassy Track: General 88, Overseas Koreans 7, R-GKS 61; 130 University Track: UIC 100, Associate Degree 30), so adding more universities does not create more places
Final results come from NIIED in December, so keep any parallel university admissions compatible with that timeline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Embassy Track: submit online on studyinkorea.go.kr in September, then embassy screening, NIIED review and the university decision; University Track: apply directly to the GKS university during September-November, then university screening and NIIED review, with NIIED announcing final results in December.
